steps.title: Wait for a condition instead of a duration

content.value:
WaitUntilCommand waits until a BooleanSupplier returns true, then finishes.

Unlike WaitCommand, which waits a fixed number of milliseconds, WaitUntilCommand waits for something to happen — a sensor reading, an encoder count, or any condition you can check.

Declare a private DcMotor field.

In initialize(), get "front_left_motor" from hardwareMap.

steps.title: Wait until the encoder counts up

content.value:
Create a SequentialCommandGroup with three commands: an InstantCommand that sets motor power to 0.5, a WaitUntilCommand with the condition () -> motor.getCurrentPosition() > 500, and an InstantCommand that stops the motor.

Schedule the group.

The motor runs until its encoder passes 500 ticks, then stops — regardless of how long that takes.

WaitCommand waits a fixed time. WaitUntilCommand waits for a condition.

Use WaitUntilCommand when the duration depends on the robot's state — like waiting for a limit switch to trigger, a sensor to detect an object, or the motor to reach a position. The condition is checked every tick.
